title: Count Special Triplets
summary: Given an integer array, count the number of triplets (i, j, k) where 0 <= i < j < k < n, and nums[i] equals nums[j] times two, and nums[k] equals nums[j] times two.
statement: Given an integer array, count the number of triplets (i, j, k) where 0 <= i < j < k < n, and nums[i] equals nums[j] times two, and nums[k] equals nums[j] times two. Return the count modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Count indices i<j<k where both outer values equal twice the middle value.
hints: For a fixed middle index, every earlier doubled value can pair with every later doubled value.
Maintain value frequencies on the left and right while moving the middle from left to right.
Remove the middle from right, add left[2*x]*right[2*x], then add it to left.
The two counters enforce index order, and their frequency product counts every valid choice of outer indices exactly once at its middle.
editorial: The two counters enforce index order, and their frequency product counts every valid choice of outer indices exactly once at its middle.

tests.explanation: The sole index triple has both outer values equal to twice three.
Indices 0, 2, and 3 form the one valid all-zero triplet.
